grammarOverrides.from: In a French pronominal verb, the reflexive pronoun agrees with the subject: je me lève, tu te réveilles, Ana se douche, nous nous préparons. Me, te and se contract to m’, t’ and s’ before a vowel. The verb also changes with its subject. Se lever and se coucher take a grave accent in the je/tu/il/ils forms (je me lève, il se couche); nous nous levons keeps the stem without that accent. For clock time use à sept heures.
grammarOverrides.to: In a French pronominal verb, the reflexive pronoun agrees with the subject: je me lève, tu te réveilles, Ana se douche, nous nous préparons. Me, te and se contract to m’, t’ and s’ before a vowel. The verb also changes with its subject. Se lever changes e to è in the je/tu/il/ils forms (je me lève); nous nous levons keeps e. Se coucher does not undergo that accent change: il se couche. For clock time use à sept heures.
grammarOverrides.reason: Correct inaccurate se coucher accent rule

cautionOverrides.from: Spanish este/ese distinguishes distance within the adjective; French ce/cette/ces alone does not. Do not use ce as a standalone “that one”: choose celui-là or celle-là.
cautionOverrides.to: Ce, cet, cette and ces do not by themselves distinguish near from far. Add -ci or -là after the noun, or use celui-là/celle-là when the noun is omitted.

cautionOverrides.from: Spanish en covers several locations. In French choose à, dans or sur by meaning. “The classroom is on the second floor” is au deuxième étage, not sur le deuxième étage.
cautionOverrides.to: Choose à, dans or sur by meaning. “The classroom is on the second floor” is au deuxième étage, not sur le deuxième étage.
